learningObjective: Reason about the trade-off between compilation-time budget and end-to-end wall-clock savings across serving scenarios.
stem: A compiler exposes a knob 'tuning budget' (compilation time spent tuning) that trades off against runtime speed. Which statements about the trade-off are TRUE? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: For a model served millions of times per day, a longer tuning budget (hours) is easily amortized over serving lifetime; the wall-clock saving per request compounds.
For a one-off ad-hoc experiment (compile, run once, discard), tuning budget must be short; a slow compile that saves runtime only matters if runtime dominates.

Recompilation on shape changes (e.g., under `torch.compile` with recompiles enabled) can inflate the effective 'compile budget' well beyond the initial compile; the effective budget is per unique shape combination the runtime sees.
Tuning budget only affects the compiler and is orthogonal to serving latency; end-to-end latency is unaffected by tuning budget once the artifact is compiled.
If the tuner reaches diminishing returns after N trials, running for 10×N trials guarantees a proportional 10× speedup.

explanation: A and B are the fundamental amortization argument. C captures an important practical concern: recompilation costs are hidden 'compile budget' spent per unique shape/config the runtime encounters. D is false: tuning budget affects the artifact's runtime performance, which is precisely serving latency. E is false: tuning curves are typically sub-linear or convex — diminishing returns mean spending 10× more time yields a marginal improvement, not 10× speedup.

optionExplanations.B: Correct: short-lived usage inverts the trade-off.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: recompilation is a hidden compile-budget line item.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: tuning budget determines the artifact's runtime performance.
optionExplanations.E: Wrong: diminishing returns invalidate proportional-speedup extrapolation.

assumptions: The tuner and cost model behave as documented (convergent search).
nonImplications: Does not imply that longer budgets always improve runtime; measurement noise and cost-model plateaus can cap gains.
Does not imply short budgets are always sufficient — some workloads need substantial trials to leave a bad local optimum.

distractorRationales.D: Denies the causal path from tuning to runtime.
